newsitem.title: INDIA: India TELCO 6-mth profits enthuse market.
newsitem.headline: India TELCO 6-mth profits enthuse market.

text.p: India's largest truck-maker, Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company (TELCO) reported better than expected first half 1996/97 results on Friday, buoying market spirits, analysts said.
"The results are definitely above market expectations. It is a good performance," said Anupam Thareja, automobile sector analyst at securities firm James Capel B&K.
TELCO said its net profit jumped 46 percent to 3.30 billion rupees in the six months to September 30, 1996 from 2.26 billion in the same period last year.
"It's a good show...," said Sandeep Talwar, auto analyst at SSKI Securities, a domestic brokerage firm.
A Reuter poll in September of 14 leading securities houses had forecast a consensus net profit of 3.26 billion rupees.
Analysts said better price realisations and improved margins were the major factors contributing to TELCO's better showing.
"Higher realisations have boosted sales," said auto analyst Sangeeta Mehta at Kotak Securities. "The critical point is that real growth has come from better operating margins."
The company said its profit before tax rose 57 percent to 47.25 million rupees from 30.15 million in the previous year.
"Better cost controls and product mix have helped TELCO boost its bottomline," said Thareja. The company's recent price hike helped push its net up, he said.
The company said its total vehicle sales increased to 99,261 in the year ending September 1996 from 81,260 last year. TELCO's net sales grew to 46.61 billion from 33.86 billion last year.

"Firm demand for the company's product range continues," TELCO Chairman Ratan Tata said in a statement. "The company set new records in levels of production and sales in any first half period in its history."
But, analysts said, a recent slowdown in industrial growth and a liquidity crunch that has affected companies could hit demand for TELCO's products in the six months to March 1997.
"These kinds of high growth are not going to be repeated. Margins are bound to come under pressure," Thareja said.
The industrial production index grew 8.5 percent in the first quarter of 1996/97 (April-March), versus 14.7 percent in the first quarter of 1995-96, India's central bank said.
"No doubt, we are seeing signs of an economic slowdown, but to what extent is a critical factor," Kotak's Mehta said.
TELCO's chairman Tata, too, anticipated these problems.
"Any significant slowdown in economic activity or a reversal of the recent easing in interest rates and liquidity could impact demand levels in the automobile sector," he said.
Thareja said the slowdown was not likely to affect TELCO's superior performance in a big way.
"There are no panic signals yet. It's not that worrying."
